To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The critical exponents are not affected by the defect, (2) The central charge is discontinuous at the critical point, (3) The defect exponents are continuous, (4) The defect expositions are continuous at the critical point.
the critical behavior of a system with defects depends on the defect structure and is different from the bulk behavior if and only if there is an incommensurate structure of defects.
the critical properties of the quantum Ising chain with defects can be determined exactly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems.
the study of the Ising quantum chain (IQC) with n arbitrarily placed impurities.
the problem of the exact solution of a quantum chain with n defects at arbitrary distances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ising chain with defects is a conformally invariant model, but the central charge and the critical exponents depend on the positions of defects.
there exists a unique critical point for the Ising chain with defects, which can be reached by varying the defect positions.
the quantum Ising chain with n defects is critical if and only if it is commensurate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we found the exact solutions for the Ising quantum chains with defects.
the Ising model with defects can be exactly solved by the algebraic Bethe ansatz method, which is a powerful method in the study of integrable models.
, the Ising quantum chain has been solved exactly in the case of arbitrary number and positions of defects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conformal invariance is a bulk property of the model and not a boundary one, and that the critical exponents are not the boundary ones.
the central charge of the Ising model is discontinuous at defect positions.
the conformal anomaly is a function of the defect structure and not just the number of defects, as has often been assumed.
